headline: Strong Topline Beat; Margin Pressure Persists

highlights: Key Points  2QFY27 revenue grew 101.6% YoY / 12.9% QoQ to Rs8,365mn, 6.4% above our estimate, driven by the INA3 ramp-up and healthy execution of the ~2.2GW order book despite slower industry installations after the ALMM List-II waiver deadline. 1HFY27 revenue grew 103.1% YoY.  EBITDA rose only 13.0% YoY to Rs633mn, with margin declining by 593bps YoY to 7.6%, below our 12.6% estimate.

Management expects EBITDA margin to reach ~20% once the cell plant is fully operational.  We maintain BUY with a revised TP of Rs114 (from Rs141), valuing the stock at 5.0x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA (from 5.5x); we cut FY27E/FY28E EBITDA by 9.6%/0.4% and PAT by 14.7%/6.9%.
Outlook: INAL continues to prioritise volume growth, with ~1.3GW of its ~2.2GW order book due for delivery by Mar_27.

Margin recovery will hinge on non-DCR pricing and the timely commissioning of the 4.5GW cell plant in 4QFY27, which should enable a shift to higher-margin DCR modules; the management expects margins to improve over the next two quarters and reach ~20% once the plant is fully operational.
valuation: Management expects EBITDA margin to reach ~20% once the cell plant is fully operational.  We maintain BUY with a revised TP of Rs114 (from Rs141), valuing the stock at 5.0x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA (from 5.5x); we cut FY27E/FY28E EBITDA by 9.6%/0.4% and PAT by 14.7%/6.9%.

Valuation: We lower our valuation multiple from 5.5x to 5.0x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA, factoring in near-term margin pressures, elevated leverage, and execution risks associated with the ongoing capacity expansion.
We maintain our BUY rating, with a revised TP of Rs114 (from Rs141), implying a ~63% upside.

Key Points  2QFY27 revenue grew 101.6% YoY / 12.9% QoQ to Rs8,365mn, 6.4% above our estimate, driven by the INA3 ramp-up and healthy execution of the ~2.2GW order book despite slower industry installations after the ALMM List-II waiver deadline. 1HFY27 revenue grew 103.1% YoY.  EBITDA rose only 13.0% YoY to Rs633mn, with margin declining by 593bps YoY to 7.6%, below our 12.6% estimate. Gross margin contracted by ~272bps QoQ to 13.5% as weak non-DCR realisations and higher traded purchases weighed, with INAL still sourcing all its cells externally.  PAT declined 32.3% YoY / 34.1% QoQ to Rs251mn (margin: 3.0%), 56.7% below our estimate, impacted by higher depreciation (Rs177mn vs Rs63mn) and finance costs (Rs128mn vs Rs47mn) from the capacity build-out, lower other income, and a higher ETR of 24.0%.  Backward integration on track: The 4.5GW cell plant is targeted for 4QFY27 with 60–70% of machinery in place, while the aluminium frame unit should start by Dec-26. Management expects EBITDA margin to reach ~20% once the cell plant is fully operational.  We maintain BUY with a revised TP of Rs114 (from Rs141), valuing the stock at 5.0x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA (from 5.5x); we cut FY27E/FY28E EBITDA by 9.6%/0.4% and PAT by 14.7%/6.9%. Outlook: INAL continues to prioritise volume growth, with ~1.3GW of its ~2.2GW order book due for delivery by Mar_27. Margin recovery will hinge on non-DCR pricing and the timely commissioning of the 4.5GW cell plant in 4QFY27, which should enable a shift to higher-margin DCR modules; the management expects margins to improve over the next two quarters and reach ~20% once the plant is fully operational. Gross debt increased to Rs14,648mn in Sep-26 (Rs8,348mn in Mar-26), driven by capex on the cell plant (CWIP Rs2,082mn vs Rs729mn; capital advances Rs2,460mn) and a stretch in working capital, with receivables nearly doubling to Rs5,377mn and inventories rising to Rs4,603mn. 1HFY27 operating cash flow was negative at Rs809mn. Management expects debt-to-equity to rise to up to 2.5x during the expansion phase before settling at 2x or below. Valuation: We lower our valuation multiple from 5.5x to 5.0x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA, factoring in near-term margin pressures, elevated leverage, and execution risks associated with the ongoing capacity expansion. We maintain a cautious stance on the pace of margin recovery despite the expected benefits of backward integration. We maintain our BUY rating, with a revised TP of Rs114 (from Rs141), implying a ~63% upside.
